## ✨ Highlights

- 🔐 **The Controller's TLS identity renews itself**: it keeps a CA of its own now (20 years, its key sealed with the master key), which signs its certificate and renews it 35 days before it ends. Nodes, the Let's Encrypt relay and janusctl check the Controller with that CA, so a renewal changes nothing for them. Before, the identity was a certificate valid a year that nothing renewed ([#451](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/451), fixes [#134](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/134)).
- 🗝️ **Renew the fleet's issuing CA with the recovery kit**: the issuing CA lasts two years. From 180 days before its end, the Fleet card asks for it: the kit and its passphrase make a new issuing CA, the Controller brings every node to a bundle listing both, then signs janusctl's certificates with the new one ([#452](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/452), fixes [#135](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/135)).
- 🛑 **A reboot ends the node's BGP sessions and VRRP**: BIRD and keepalived are stopped before the node reboots or powers off, so its BGP peers drop its routes at once and keepalived hands the VIP over ([#450](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/450), fixes [#446](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/446)).

## 🔄 Since the v2026.10.31-2 pre-release

What its lab campaign found ([#453](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/453)), fixed in [#454](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/454):

- **The Fleet card shows where the nodes stand right after a renewal**: **Renew the issuing CA** and **Reach them with the recovery kit** answered before the Controller had brought the nodes the new bundle, so the card listed every node as behind until the next refresh. They now answer once that pass is done (15 seconds at most): the nodes on the new bundle, and the switch when they all have it.
- **`-advertise-address`'s first entry is where nodes register**: replacing it with a name, to give the certificate that name, moved the address nodes are told to register at. The flag's help, [the Controller's page](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/dashboard/README.md#tls-identity), the Docker Hub page and the relay's guide say to add a name after the first entry, and the Controller logs at start where nodes are told to register (`registration: nodes are told to register at ...`).

## ⚙️ Node

- **Reboot, power-off, reset, a failed boot's revert** ([#450](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/450)): after HAProxy's soft stop, the extension services stop - Consul's services in maintenance first, keepalived and BIRD last, as on a normal shutdown. The reboot line times it as "extension services". A node without extension services keeps its line as it was.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Its identity** ([#451](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/451)):
  - `dashboard-identity-ca.crt` (its key sealed with the master key) signs `dashboard-identity.crt`, valid a year and renewed by itself 35 days before its end - or at the next start when `-advertise-address` names something it doesn't cover: no more deleting the files to add a name. A renewed certificate keeps every name the one before had.
  - Nodes are given the CA: controller-info's `ca_cert_pem`, the Provision panel's `controller-ca.crt`, the NoCloud of the machines it creates, the relay's settings.
  - Nodes reaching Let's Encrypt through the relay with the certificate alone are given the CA by the Controller (every 12 hours, as `lets-encrypt`, their other settings kept).
  - **Settings › HTTPS certificate** shows the identity: its CA's fingerprint and end, the certificate's end, and a download of the CA - to install in a browser, for passkeys on a page without a certificate of its own.
  - Restoring a backup made before this release on a new Controller works: the new Controller's own identity CA, sealed with a master key the restore replaces, goes.
- **Renewing the fleet's issuing CA** ([#452](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/452)):
  - **Renew the issuing CA** on the Fleet card, with the kit and its passphrase (`POST /api/fleet/renew`): a new issuing CA named for its month, a bundle listing it and the current one.
  - The Controller keeps the bundle version each node was last seen with, and reaches each with a certificate it lets in: the CA before's until the node has the bundle, the new one's after. A node switched off throughout comes back by itself.
  - janusctl's certificates come from the new CA once every node has the bundle, or 30 days before the CA before ends. The card says where it stands.
  - A node no issuing CA reaches any more - it missed a renewal, or the CA expired - says **needs the recovery kit**: **Reach them with the recovery kit** (`POST /api/fleet/rescue`) has the Controller reach it for an hour with a certificate the root signs, and bring it to the bundle.
  - A notice on the Fleet card from 180 days before the issuing CA ends (danger in the last 30), a header badge for admins from 60 days, a log line a day.
  - No certificate is issued from an expired issuing CA any more, and none outlives its CA.
- **A node refusing the Controller's certificate** is reported as such: the Controller no longer waits for its deadline retrying a refused certificate.

## 💻 janusctl

- **A context that pinned the Controller's certificate follows its renewals** ([#451](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/451)): every sign-in (API token, SSH key, browser, device) gives janusctl the identity's CA, which it keeps (`controller_identity_ca`) and checks the next certificate with. A `-controller-ca` of yours keeps checking the name dialed.
- An SSH sign-in begun just before a renewal still goes through.

- [The Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/dashboard/README.md#renewing-the-issuing-ca): renewing the issuing CA; the identity, the CA to give Terraform, Prometheus and scripts.

## 🧪 Tests

- `qemu-self-register-test` provisions the node with the identity CA alone. New `qemu-self-register-legacy-test`: a node provisioned by a Controller made before this release registers after the Controller switched to a certificate its CA signs.
- `qemu-dashboard-test` renews the identity (a pinned janusctl context follows) and the fleet's issuing CA (the real node takes the bundle, janusctl's certificates switch, the Controller keeps reaching the node across a restart).
- `qemu-cluster-upgrade-bgp-test`'s router is back on BIRD's own timers, and checks a rebooting member's session ends before it listens again ([#450](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/450)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **A Controller from before this release keeps serving its first certificate** until 35 days before it ends (its log and Settings › HTTPS certificate give the date), then serves one its CA signs. Browsers ask once more then. janusctl contexts and the relay's nodes follow by themselves after this update; give the CA (controller-info's `ca_cert_pem`, or **Download the identity CA**) to whatever else was given that certificate before the switch: Terraform's `ca_cert`, Prometheus's `ca_file`, scripts, and a seeded image or a saved NoCloud user-data of a node not registered yet.
- **Rolling the Controller back** after a renewal of the issuing CA keeps working: the older release signs with the CA janusctl's certificates come from.
- **To give the Controller's certificate another name**, add it to `-advertise-address` after the first entry, not in its place: the first is the address nodes are told to register at.
- **Back up the Controller after renewing the issuing CA**: a backup from before brings the old CA back - it keeps working while that CA lasts, then renew again.
